newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rabin killer says it felt like killing a terrorist.
newsitem.headline: Rabin killer says it felt like killing a terrorist.

text.p: The religious Jew who killed Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin to halt peace moves with the Arabs told a state inquiry into the assassination he felt he was shooting a "terrorist", an Israeli newspaper said on Thursday.

"When I fired (at Rabin) I felt like I was firing at a terrorist," Yigal Amir said, according to the Yedioth Ahronoth daily, printing what it said were excerpts from his testimony. "I am unable to kill innocent people."
Ultra-nationalist Amir, 27, is serving a life sentence for shooting Rabin at a Tel Aviv peace rally on November 4, 1995 after stalking him for months.
Rabin shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994 for reaching an accord with arch-PLO rival Yasser Arafat that launched Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
His assassination set Israel on a path to new elections in which right-wing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ousted Rabin's Labour party.
Amir said in a documentary film screened last week that Netanyahu was a "cynical opportunist" but was still better than his Labour predecessors.
